title.es: Señalizar el recorrido de una charla

es: Reconocer y ordenar las expresiones que señalizan la apertura, las transiciones y el cierre de una charla, y elegir la fórmula adecuada para cada momento.

teaching.en: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to present the results of our neighbourhood survey.
teaching.es: Buenos días a todos. Hoy quiero presentar los resultados de nuestra encuesta del barrio.
teaching.explanationEs: Apertura: saludo + Today I want to present… anuncia el tema de la charla.
segments: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to
present the results of our neighbourhood survey.
teaching.audioText: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to present the results of our neighbourhood survey.

teaching.en: I will outline the talk in three parts, and firstly I will explain how we collected the data.
teaching.es: Expondré la charla en tres partes y, en primer lugar, explicaré cómo recogimos los datos.
teaching.explanationEs: I will outline… anuncia el esquema; firstly abre la primera parte.
segments: I will outline the talk in three parts, and
firstly I will explain how we collected the data.
teaching.audioText: I will outline the talk in three parts, and firstly I will explain how we collected the data.

teaching.en: Let's move on to the results.
teaching.es: Pasemos a los resultados.
teaching.explanationEs: Transición: Let's move on to + parte; en inglés no se dice «pass to».
segments: Let's move on
to the results.
teaching.audioText: Let's move on to the results.

teaching.en: Now I'd like to turn to the question of noise.
teaching.es: Ahora me gustaría pasar al tema del ruido.
teaching.explanationEs: Now I'd like to turn to + tema: transición algo más formal.
segments: Now I'd like to turn
to the question of noise.
teaching.audioText: Now I'd like to turn to the question of noise.

teaching.en: To sum up, most neighbours want safer streets and quieter nights.
teaching.es: En resumen, la mayoría de los vecinos quiere calles más seguras y noches más tranquilas.
teaching.explanationEs: Cierre: To sum up, + la idea principal, en una o dos frases.
segments: To sum up, most neighbours want
safer streets and quieter nights.
teaching.audioText: To sum up, most neighbours want safer streets and quieter nights.

teaching.en: Finally, I will take any questions you may have.
teaching.es: Por último, responderé a las preguntas que tengan.
teaching.explanationEs: Finally anuncia el último paso; después se invita a hacer preguntas.
segments: Finally, I will take any
questions you may have.
teaching.audioText: Finally, I will take any questions you may have.

prompt.es: Elige la expresión que abre una charla anunciando el tema.

choices.text: To sum up, our survey shows the results.
Let's move on to the next point.
Today I want to present our survey of the neighbourhood.

feedback.es: Today I want to present… abre la charla y anuncia el tema; To sum up la cierra y Let's move on pasa de un punto a otro.

hint.es: La apertura dice de qué vas a hablar; no resume ni cambia de punto.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ahora quiero pasar al tema del tráfico.»

feedback.es: Turn to + tema es la fórmula para pasar a otro asunto: Now I'd like to turn to… El verbo turn va seguido de to.

origin.text: Now I'd like to ___ to the question of traffic.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Pasemos ahora a la segunda parte.»

answer.text: Let's move on to the second part

feedback.es: Let's move on to + parte es la transición natural; en inglés no se dice pass to. La segunda parte cierra la frase.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con el momento de la charla.

pairs: Welcome, everyone. I'd like to talk about our local park.
Now let's turn to the cost of the project.
Finally, let me thank you all for coming.

feedback.es: Welcome, everyone abre la charla, Now let's turn to… pasa a otro punto y Finally, let me thank… la cierra.

pairs: Welcome, everyone. I'd like to talk about our local park.
Now let's turn to the cost of the project.
Finally, let me thank you all for coming.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el orden de las tres partes de la charla.

choices.text: The problem, the survey and then a proposal.
A proposal, the problem and then the survey.
The survey, a proposal and then the problem.

feedback.es: La oradora anuncia primero el problema (firstly), después la encuesta (secondly) y al final una propuesta (finally): ese es el orden de las partes.

origin.audio: Good afternoon. I will outline my talk in three parts. Firstly, the problem; secondly, our survey; and finally, a proposal.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para resumir, el barrio necesita más zonas verdes.»

feedback.es: To sum up + idea principal es la fórmula de cierre más habitual; sum va entre to y up.

origin.text: To ___ up, the neighbourhood needs more green spaces.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su función en la charla.

pairs: I will outline the talk in two parts.
Now let's move on to the costs.
To sum up, the plan is realistic.

feedback.es: Cada expresión cumple un papel distinto: saludar, anunciar el esquema, pasar a otro punto, resumir y cerrar con agradecimiento.

pairs: I will outline the talk in two parts.
Now let's move on to the costs.
To sum up, the plan is realistic.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué hablará la oradora después de la encuesta.

choices.text: What the audience wants to ask.
How much the bike lane will cost.
Where the survey took place.

feedback.es: La oradora dice que empezará con la encuesta y después pasará al coste (move on to the cost): el siguiente tema es cuánto costará el carril.

origin.audio: Thank you all for coming. Today I will outline our plan for a new bike lane. I will start with the survey, then move on to the cost, and finish with your questions.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por último, quiero agradecerles su atención.»

feedback.es: Finally (o lastly) introduce el último paso de la charla, justo antes de agradecer o de abrir las preguntas.

origin.text: ___, I would like to thank you for your attention.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hoy quiero presentar los resultados de nuestra encuesta.»

answer.text: Today I want to present our survey results

feedback.es: Today I want to present + resultados abre la charla con el tema: el verbo present va después de want to.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que sirve para cerrar una charla.

choices.text: Firstly, I will describe the method.
Now I'd like to turn to the results.
To sum up, the survey shows that people want change.

feedback.es: To sum up + idea principal cierra la charla; Firstly la abre y Now I'd like to turn to… cambia de tema en medio.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la frase inicial del audio.

choices.text: It moves the talk to a new topic.
It closes the talk with a summary.
It opens the talk with a greeting.

feedback.es: Now I'd like to turn to… es una transición: lleva la charla a un tema nuevo, el tráfico; no saluda ni cierra.

origin.audio: Now I'd like to turn to the main problem: traffic. According to the survey, most people say it is too heavy in the morning.

prompt.es: Completa: «Pasemos ahora a la última parte.»

feedback.es: Let's move on to + parte es la transición habitual; move va antes de on to.

origin.text: Let's ___ on to the last part.

es: Describir cifras y tendencias de un gráfico con verbos de cambio, adverbios de intensidad y aproximaciones (rose sharply, a steady rise, roughly, just under).

teaching.en: Bus use rose sharply in March, from 2,000 to 3,500 passengers.
teaching.es: El uso del autobús subió bruscamente en marzo, de 2.000 a 3.500 pasajeros.
teaching.explanationEs: Rose sharply: verbo de subida + adverbio de intensidad; from… to… da el punto de partida y de llegada.
segments: Bus use rose sharply in March,
from 2,000 to 3,500 passengers.
teaching.audioText: Bus use rose sharply in March, from 2,000 to 3,500 passengers.

teaching.en: The number of cyclists fell slightly between May and June.
teaching.es: El número de ciclistas bajó ligeramente entre mayo y junio.
teaching.explanationEs: Slightly describe un cambio pequeño; fell es el pasado de fall.
segments: The number of cyclists fell
slightly between May and June.
teaching.audioText: The number of cyclists fell slightly between May and June.

teaching.en: Train use grew gradually over the whole year.
teaching.es: El uso del tren creció poco a poco durante todo el año.
teaching.explanationEs: Gradually: cambio lento y continuo; el periodo terminado va en pasado.
segments: Train use grew gradually
over the whole year.
teaching.audioText: Train use grew gradually over the whole year.

teaching.en: There was a steady rise in tram passengers, from 900 to 1,200.
teaching.es: Hubo una subida constante de pasajeros de tranvía, de 900 a 1.200.
teaching.explanationEs: There was a steady rise: sustantivo de tendencia con adjetivo; steady = sin saltos.
segments: There was a steady rise in
tram passengers, from 900 to 1,200.
teaching.audioText: There was a steady rise in tram passengers, from 900 to 1,200.

teaching.en: Roughly 40 percent of passengers travel at peak times.
teaching.es: Aproximadamente el 40 % de los pasajeros viaja en hora punta.
teaching.explanationEs: Roughly + cifra: aproximación; se puede cambiar por around o about.
segments: Roughly 40 percent of passengers
travel at peak times.
teaching.audioText: Roughly 40 percent of passengers travel at peak times.

teaching.en: The figure for taxis will remain steady at around 500 a day.
teaching.es: La cifra de taxis seguirá estable en torno a 500 al día.
teaching.explanationEs: Remain + adjetivo: la cifra no cambia; figure es la cifra o el dato numérico.
segments: The figure for taxis will remain
steady at around 500 a day.
teaching.audioText: The figure for taxis will remain steady at around 500 a day.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe una subida fuerte y rápida.

choices.text: Cycling rose sharply from 100 to 400 riders.
Cycling rose slightly from 100 to 400 riders.
Cycling remained steady at 100 riders.

feedback.es: Sharply indica un cambio brusco: de 100 a 400 es una subida muy fuerte. Slightly describe un cambio pequeño y remained steady, ausencia de cambio.

hint.es: Cuadruplicar una cifra es un cambio grande y rápido.

origin.text: Cycling: 100 riders in April, 400 in May.

prompt.es: Completa: «El número de pasajeros cayó poco a poco durante el año.»

feedback.es: Gradually es el adverbio de un cambio lento y continuo; va después del verbo y antes del periodo.

hint.es: Adverbio de un cambio lento, paso a paso.

origin.text: The number of passengers fell ___ during the year.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hubo una subida constante en el uso del coche.»

answer.text: There was a steady rise in car use

feedback.es: A steady rise combina un sustantivo de tendencia con un adjetivo de intensidad: una subida sin saltos; después va in + lo que se mide.

hint.es: Empieza con There was a steady.

prompt.es: Elige la aproximación que encaja con los datos.

choices.text: Just over half of the people use the bus.
Just under half of the people use the bus.
Roughly a quarter of the people use the bus.

feedback.es: 98 de 200 es el 49 %: just under half. Just over half sería más del 50 % y roughly a quarter, un 25 %.

origin.text: In a survey of 200 people, 98 said they use the bus.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ocurrió con los turistas en mayo.

choices.text: The number went up slowly.
The number stayed the same.
The number fell quickly.

feedback.es: El audio dice que la cifra dropped sharply en mayo: una caída brusca. La subida gradual fue antes, de enero a abril.

origin.audio: Between January and April the number of tourists rose gradually, from about one hundred to around two hundred and fifty. Then it dropped sharply in May.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hubo una gran caída en el uso del taxi.»

feedback.es: Drop (o fall) es un sustantivo de tendencia: a big drop es una gran caída y va seguido de in + lo que se mide.

origin.text: There was a big ___ in taxi use.

prompt.es: Elige la descripción correcta de las ventas.

choices.text: Sales remained steady at around 1,000.
Sales rose sharply in August.
Sales dropped gradually in July.

feedback.es: De 1,000 a 1,010 el cambio es mínimo: las ventas se mantuvieron estables. Sharply y dropped no encajan con esos datos.

origin.text: Sales: 1,000 in June, 1,000 in July, 1,010 in August.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la descripción correcta de los socios.

choices.text: Less than half are under thirty, and a quarter are over fifty.
More than half are under thirty, and about a quarter are over fifty.
Most members are over fifty.

feedback.es: Nearly sixty percent es más de la mitad y just under a quarter es casi el veinticinco por ciento: aproximadamente un cuarto.

origin.audio: Nearly sixty percent of the members are under thirty, and just under a quarter are over fifty.

prompt.es: Completa las dos frases con el adverbio o la aproximación adecuados.

feedback.es: Slightly describe una subida de solo dos euros y just under (o nearly, almost) aproxima 49 sobre 100 a la mitad.

sentences: ___ half of the visitors are women: 49 out of 100.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los precios se mantuvieron estables todo el año.»

feedback.es: Remained steady describe una cifra que no cambia; remain se construye con un adjetivo y el periodo va al final.

prompt.es: Elige la versión correcta: «El número de visitantes aumentó un 10 %.»

choices.text: The number of visitors increased of 10 percent.
The number of visitors increased in 10 percent.
The number of visitors increased by 10 percent.

feedback.es: Después de increase, by indica cuánto cambia la cifra. Las versiones con of o in son calcos del español.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué pasó con los visitantes en diciembre.

choices.text: It went up a little.
It fell sharply.
It stayed exactly the same.

feedback.es: El audio dice que la cifra rose slightly en diciembre: una subida pequeña. Antes estaba estable en unos cuatrocientos por semana.

origin.audio: The figure for museum visitors was steady at around four hundred a week, and then it rose slightly in December.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada adverbio con su significado.

feedback.es: Estos adverbios gradúan la tendencia o la cifra: sharply es brusco, gradually es poco a poco, slightly es un poco y roughly aproxima.

title.en: Follow the structure of a talk
title.es: Seguir la estructura de una charla

es: Seguir la estructura de una charla en audio (apertura, puntos principales y cierre) y anotar sus puntos clave a partir de las señales del orador.

teaching.en: I will cover three main points: cost, safety and comfort.
teaching.es: Trataré tres puntos principales: el coste, la seguridad y la comodidad.
teaching.explanationEs: Cover + main points: el orador anuncia el esquema; anota cuántos puntos son.
segments: I will cover three main
points: cost, safety and comfort.
teaching.audioText: I will cover three main points: cost, safety and comfort.

teaching.en: The first key point is cost: a monthly ticket now costs forty euros.
teaching.es: El primer punto clave es el coste: un billete mensual cuesta ahora cuarenta euros.
teaching.explanationEs: The first key point is… abre el punto 1; después viene un dato para anotar.
segments: The first key point is cost: a
monthly ticket now costs forty euros.
teaching.audioText: The first key point is cost: a monthly ticket now costs forty euros.

teaching.en: Briefly, the second point is safety, and the new buses have better lights.
teaching.es: En pocas palabras, el segundo punto es la seguridad, y los autobuses nuevos tienen mejores luces.
teaching.explanationEs: Briefly avisa de que el punto será corto; el número de punto sigue en el mismo orden.
segments: Briefly, the second point is safety, and
the new buses have better lights.
teaching.audioText: Briefly, the second point is safety, and the new buses have better lights.

teaching.en: To recap, a clear structure helps the audience follow the talk.
teaching.es: Para repasar, una estructura clara ayuda al público a seguir la charla.
teaching.explanationEs: To recap señala el cierre: empieza el resumen de los puntos.
segments: To recap, a clear structure helps
the audience follow the talk.
teaching.audioText: To recap, a clear structure helps the audience follow the talk.

teaching.en: I note each key word in my notebook while I listen.
teaching.es: Anoto cada palabra clave en mi cuaderno mientras escucho.
teaching.explanationEs: Note: anota solo palabras clave, no frases completas.
segments: I note each key word in
my notebook while I listen.
teaching.audioText: I note each key word in my notebook while I listen.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué trata la charla y cuántos puntos tiene.

choices.text: A school trip, with two activities.
A school library, in three parts.
A school canteen, in four parts.

feedback.es: La oradora dice que tratará tres puntos principales sobre la biblioteca del colegio: horario, libros y espacios de estudio.

hint.es: Escucha la señal de apertura: dice el tema y cuántos puntos anuncia.

origin.audio: Hello, everyone. Today I will cover three main points about our school library: opening hours, books and study spaces.

prompt.es: Completa: «El primer punto clave es el horario.»

feedback.es: The first key point is… abre el primer punto; key (o main) es el adjetivo que lo marca como importante.

origin.text: The first ___ point is opening hours.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Para repasar, la charla tiene tres partes.»

answer.text: To recap the talk has three parts

feedback.es: To recap + idea es la señal de cierre: va al principio, y después viene lo que se resume.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quieren muchos estudiantes.

choices.text: More books about history.
A quieter reading room.
A later closing time.

feedback.es: El audio dice que la biblioteca cierra a las cuatro y que muchos estudiantes querrían que siguiera abierta hasta las siete: quieren un cierre más tarde.

origin.audio: The first key point is opening hours. At the moment, the library closes at four o'clock, and many students would like it to stay open until seven.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del orador con su función.

pairs: I will cover three main points.
To recap, we need longer hours.
The second key point is space.

feedback.es: I will cover anuncia el esquema, To recap abre el cierre y The second key point is… abre el punto dos.

pairs: I will cover three main points.
To recap, we need longer hours.
The second key point is space.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dato se da sobre el espacio de estudio.

choices.text: There are very few desks for so many students.
There are too many desks for the students.
There is a new study room for everyone.

feedback.es: El audio dice que hay solo doce mesas para ochocientos estudiantes: muy pocas mesas para tantos alumnos.

origin.audio: Briefly, the second key point is study space. There are only twelve desks for eight hundred students.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el segundo punto que anuncia la oradora.

choices.text: The safety.
The cost.
The health.

feedback.es: La oradora enumera safety, cost y health; el punto que va en medio, justo después de la seguridad, es el coste.

origin.audio: Good morning. My talk is about cycling to school, and I will cover three main points: safety, cost and health.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la oradora al final del audio.

choices.text: She introduces a new main point.
She asks the audience to leave.
She summarises the whole talk.

feedback.es: To recap anuncia un resumen: la oradora repite los puntos de la charla en vez de presentar uno nuevo.

origin.audio: A bicycle is cheaper than a bus pass after one year, and students who cycle arrive more awake. To recap, cycling is good for health, cheaper than the bus and safer with a bike lane.

prompt.es: Completa: «Voy a abordar solo dos puntos principales.»

feedback.es: Cover significa tratar un tema en una charla; I will cover + número + main points anuncia el esquema.

origin.text: I will ___ only two main points.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Brevemente, el tercer punto clave es la salud.»

answer.text: Briefly the third key point is health

feedback.es: Briefly abre la frase y avisa de que el punto será corto; después va el número de punto y el tema.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué parte de la charla es este fragmento.

choices.text: The closing.
The opening.
The second main point.

feedback.es: In short… y la invitación a hacer preguntas son típicas del cierre: la oradora resume el plan y abre el turno de preguntas.

origin.audio: Thank you for listening. In short, the plan has three parts: a bike lane, cheaper tickets and safer crossings. Now, are there any questions?

prompt.es: ¿Qué función tiene «To recap» en este fragmento?

choices.text: It opens the second point.
It starts the closing summary.
It introduces the speaker.

feedback.es: To recap señala el cierre: resume los puntos principales; no abre un punto nuevo ni presenta al orador.

origin.text: To recap, the library needs longer hours, more desks and quieter rooms. Thank you.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada palabra con su significado en una charla.

feedback.es: Cover significa tratar un tema, briefly dice que será corto y recap indica que se repasa lo dicho.

title.es: Guion de una charla de dos minutos

es: Escribir el guion de una charla de dos minutos sobre un tema personal, con una apertura clara, al menos tres señalizadores, una tendencia descrita con cifras y un cierre.

teaching.en: A two-minute talk has about two hundred words, so the script must be short and clear.
teaching.es: Una charla de dos minutos tiene unas doscientas palabras, así que el guion debe ser corto y claro.
teaching.explanationEs: Script: el texto que escribes para decir en voz alta; frases cortas, una idea por frase.
segments: A two-minute talk has about two hundred words,
so the script must be short and clear.
teaching.audioText: A two-minute talk has about two hundred words, so the script must be short and clear.

teaching.en: She begins by greeting the audience and naming her topic.
teaching.es: Ella empieza saludando al público y nombrando su tema.
teaching.explanationEs: Apertura: saludo + tema; el público debe saber de qué vas a hablar.
segments: She begins by greeting the
audience and naming her topic.
teaching.audioText: She begins by greeting the audience and naming her topic.

teaching.en: She will introduce each point with a phrase such as firstly or now let's move on.
teaching.es: Presentará cada punto con una frase como «firstly» o «now let's move on».
teaching.explanationEs: Introduce each point: los señalizadores de la clase 86 sirven para esto.
segments: She will introduce each point with a phrase
such as firstly or now let's move on.
teaching.audioText: She will introduce each point with a phrase such as firstly or now let's move on.

teaching.en: Her script describes a trend: the number of members rose from twelve to thirty in a year.
teaching.es: Su guion describe una tendencia: el número de socios subió de doce a treinta en un año.
teaching.explanationEs: La tendencia lleva un verbo de cambio, from… to… y un periodo.
segments: Her script describes a trend: the number of members
rose from twelve to thirty in a year.
teaching.audioText: Her script describes a trend: the number of members rose from twelve to thirty in a year.

teaching.en: A good speaker keeps a steady pace and makes a short pause after each key point.
teaching.es: Un buen orador mantiene un ritmo constante y hace una breve pausa después de cada punto clave.
teaching.explanationEs: Pace: velocidad al hablar; pause: parada breve que deja pensar al público.
segments: A good speaker keeps a steady pace and
makes a short pause after each key point.
teaching.audioText: A good speaker keeps a steady pace and makes a short pause after each key point.

teaching.en: I always rehearse aloud so that my script fits into two minutes.
teaching.es: Siempre ensayo en voz alta para que mi guion quepa en dos minutos.
teaching.explanationEs: Rehearse aloud: ensayar diciendo el texto en voz alta para medir el tiempo.
segments: I always rehearse aloud so that
my script fits into two minutes.
teaching.audioText: I always rehearse aloud so that my script fits into two minutes.

prompt.es: Elige la apertura más adecuada para una charla de dos minutos.

choices.text: Hello. Football. Thank you.
To sum up, football is a great game.
Good morning, everyone. My topic is football, and I will cover three points.

feedback.es: Una buena apertura saluda, nombra el tema y anuncia cuántos puntos habrá. To sum up es una fórmula de cierre y Hello. Football. Thank you. no presenta nada.

hint.es: La apertura saluda, nombra el tema y anuncia el esquema.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es importante hacer una pausa después de cada punto.»

feedback.es: Make a pause significa hacer una parada breve; ayuda al público a pensar en el punto clave.

origin.text: It is important to make a ___ after each point.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ensayo en voz alta para medir el tiempo.»

answer.text: I rehearse aloud to check the time

feedback.es: I rehearse aloud es una frase en presente simple; to check the time explica para qué se ensaya.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del guion con su función.

pairs: Our club grew from 12 to 30 members.
Now let's move on to the second point.
Thank you for listening. Any questions?

feedback.es: La cifra con from… to… describe una tendencia, now let's move on es un señalizador y la despedida con preguntas cierra.

pairs: Our club grew from 12 to 30 members.
Now let's move on to the second point.
Thank you for listening. Any questions?

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe esta tendencia en el guion.

choices.text: Our club more than doubled, rising from 12 to 30 members.
Our club fell sharply from 30 to 12 members.
Our club stayed steady at 12 members.

feedback.es: Rising from 12 to 30 describe una subida con punto de partida y de llegada; more than doubled es la aproximación exacta. Las otras frases invierten o niegan los datos.

origin.text: Data: members in 2022: 12; in 2024: 30.

prompt.es: Completa: «Voy a presentar cada punto con una frase clara.»

feedback.es: Introduce each point significa presentar cada punto con una frase de transición; el verbo va después de I will.

origin.text: I will ___ each point with a clear phrase.

prompt.es: Elige el guion con mejor estructura de apertura, desarrollo y cierre.

choices.text: Swimming is fun. Thank you. Firstly, the club has twelve members.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club grew. As you can see in my chart, the number of members rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of them are first-year students, and nearly a third are boys. This suggests that the club is becoming more popular, and it may grow even more next year. Finally, let me tell you about our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew steadily and is ready for a new challenge. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.

Hello, everyone, and welcome. Today I want to present my hobby, which is running, and I will outline the talk in three parts: why I started, how my training changed and my next goal. Firstly, I started running two years ago because I wanted to feel healthier. At the beginning, I could run for only ten minutes without stopping. Let's move on to the second part: my training. As you can see in my chart, my weekly distance rose gradually, from roughly five to around twenty kilometres in one year. I also make a short pause between exercises, and I keep a steady pace. Now I'd like to turn to my goal for next year. I am likely to run a half marathon in the spring, and my friends will run with me. To sum up, running is cheap, simple and good for the head as well as for the body. Thank you very much for listening. Are there any questions?

prompt.es: Escribe tu presentación final con dos respuestas matizadas.

answer.text: To sum up my talk, I presented a study of 120 students who slept eight hours a night for a month. Their marks rose from 7.1 to 7.8, and the effect was clear for most of them. Now let me answer your two questions. First, you asked how many of the students were girls. I'm afraid I don't have the exact figure, but as far as I know it was around half, and I would need to check the report. Second, you asked whether these students were simply better students already. That is a fair challenge. To a certain extent you may be right, because the students chose to take part. Nevertheless, the marks of the same students rose during the study, so the findings suggest that sleep may help, although more research is needed. I can give you more detail after the talk. Thank you for your questions.

Let me summarise the main points of my talk. We studied 120 students for a month. Those who slept eight hours scored higher, and their mark went up from 7.1 to 7.8. Thank you for your two questions. About the first one, how many girls took part, I'm afraid I can't give an accurate number now, but I can check it and send you the figure later. About the second one, it could be argued that these students were already better, and that is a fair point. However, the same students improved during the month, so the results seem to show a real effect. It is likely to be valid for students of our age, although I would not say it is certain. I can give you more detail after the talk.
